1.explanation: All of the JavaScript highlighting logic lives in the default export of src/languages/javascript.js. In the returned grammar’s contains array there are rules for the ES6 class declaration (beginKeywords: 'class'), for the constructor, and for get/set accessors—but there is no rule to recognize and highlight arbitrary method definitions like `myMethod() {…}`. To fix the missing highlighting of member functions, you must extend the grammar inside that exported function (in javascript.js) to add a new pattern matching plain class methods.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering ES6 class code blocks through marked + highlight.js in React, plain member methods (for example “changeScrollTopShow()” or “scrollToTop()”) inside a class are never styled—only the “class” keyword, constructor and get/set accessors get highlighted. The screenshot shows an ES6 class with several methods uncoloured.

2.explanation: All of the JavaScript syntax-highlighting rules live inside the default export function of src/languages/javascript.js. That function defines patterns for free functions, the class keyword, constructors, and get/set accessors—but it never defines a pattern to recognize ordinary ES6 class methods. As a result, member functions inside a class body aren’t highlighted. The fix is to update this default language-definition function (in javascript.js) to add a rule under the class/container section that matches and highlights generic class-method definitions.
2.bug_scenario: When using highlight.js via marked in a React application to render ES6 class source code, the user’s class member methods (e.g. changeScrollTopShow, scrollToTop) are never picked up by the JavaScript grammar and so appear as plain text instead of being syntax-highlighted.
